in four intervention studies in different nonEuropean Union (EU) countries. The EFSA considers that the potential effect of physical
activity and of MTHFR 677TT genotype on riboﬂavin requirement is covered by the data presented from the studies considered, thus
is accounted for in the assumed the coefﬁcient of variation (CV) applied to set the PRI for riboﬂavin. A CV of 10% was used to
calculate PRIs from the ARs for adults, i.e., 1.6 mg day1 after rounding, and the same CV was used for all other population groups.
EFSA considers that there is no indication of different riboﬂavin requirement according to sex or between younger and older adults,
and sets the same DRV for men and women (without correction per difference in body weight) of all ages. For all infants aged 7–
11 months, in the absence of sufﬁcient data to set an AR, the EFSA sets an AI of 0.4 mg day1 based on the estimated intake of
